name: Shor

ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Turkic (South Siberian Turkic branch, closely related to Khakas).
Khakas adstrate: closely related neighbouring South Siberian Turkic language.
Russian adstrate: Soviet-era lexicon and long Siberian regional contact.

notes: Shor (шор тили), a South Siberian Turkic language of the Kemerovo region, Russia, closely related to Khakas, written in a Cyrillic alphabet: the Russian letters plus ⟨ғ⟩ /ɡ/, ⟨ң⟩ /ŋ/, ⟨ӧ⟩ /ø/, ⟨ӱ⟩ /y/, ⟨қ⟩ /k/ and the affricate letter ⟨ҷ⟩ /dʒ/. Front/back velar pairs are spelled with distinct letters: plain ⟨к⟩ and ⟨г⟩ mark the fronted (palatalised) velar/uvular allophones /c/ /ɟ/, while ⟨қ⟩ and ⟨ғ⟩ mark the back velars /k/ /ɡ/ — a genuine orthographic contrast, not an allophone rule, so both members are kept as separate graphemes (cf. Khakas, which does not distinguish this pair in spelling). Vowel length is phonemic and written by DOUBLING the vowel letter (аа ее ии оо ӧӧ уу ӱӱ ыы), listed as multigraph keys so maximal-munch matching prefers them over the single short-vowel letters. Vowel harmony (front/back, rounding) operates throughout. ⟨ф ц щ ъ ь⟩ occur mainly in Russian loanwords; the silent hard/soft signs carry no independent segment and are omitted from the grapheme map.
